pr_title: sql: `SET DEFAULT NULL` means a nil default expr instead of "NULL"
pr_body:
Previously, `SET DEFAULT NULL` resulted in a column whose DefaultExpr is "NULL". This is problematic when used with `ALTER COLUMN TYPE` where a temporary computed column will be created, hence violating validation that "a computed column cannot have default expression". This PR fixes that by setting DefaultExpr to nil when `SET DEFAULT NULL`.

Fixes #91069 
Release note (bug fix): Fixed a bug described in #91069.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/91078)

Alright never mind about ON UPDATE then.

By all means backport to release-22.1, just don't backport to release-22.2.0, that's all.

issue_context.title: Unable to alter column type with DEFAULT NULL
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Attempting to reduce the size of a fixed-size varchar column results in error message.

**To Reproduce**

```
CREATE TABLE t (
	id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
	s VARCHAR(64) NULL
);

ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN s SET DEFAULT NULL;

ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN s TYPE VARCHAR(32);
```

The final command gives this error message:

```
ERROR: relation "t" (119): computed column "s_1" cannot also have a DEFAULT expression
```

The type change works fine if I replace the `SET DEFAULT` to `DROP DEFAULT`.  Is this intended behaviour?

**Expected behavior**
The `ALTER COLUMN` should just work as the intention implies.

**Environment:**
 - Observed on all 22.1 versions.

Jira issue: CRDB-21094
comments:
Note that the following however works:

```

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> create table t2( id uuid not null default gen_random_uuid() primary key, s varchar(64) null default null);
CREATE TABLE


Time: 121ms total (execution 118ms / network 2ms)


root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> ALTER TABLE t2 ALTER COLUMN s TYPE VARCHAR(32);
NOTICE: ALTER COLUMN TYPE changes are finalized asynchronously; further schema changes on this table may be restricted until the job completes; some writes to the altered column may be rejected until the schema change is finalized
ALTER TABLE


Time: 1.727s total (execution 1.726s / network 0.001s)
```

review_comments: Dumb question perhaps but shouldn't this logic rather be in `updateNonComputedColExpr`? It feels like this should also apply to `ON UPDATE` expressions.
